# What this app is made of

A map of the code as it stands, so a question like "where does the budget
period live" or "what does Siri already answer" costs one file instead of
thirty. Hard-won facts that are **not** in the code — Sideloadly, free-account
limits, Expo quirks — live next door in [FACTS.md](FACTS.md).

At least 0 tests across 29 suites (`it.each` expands
into more; `npm test` prints the real number). 16 screens,
8 migrations.

## Database

Migrations are append-only: a shipped one is never edited. `PRAGMA user_version`
records how many have run.

| Version | What it is for                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Tables and indexes                                                                   |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| v1      | the first schema                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | +categories, +expenses, +budgets, index expenses_by_date, index expenses_by_category |
| v2      | one overall monthly budget across all categories (a single-row table).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | +overall_budget                                                                      |
| v3      | app settings (payday rule, alerts), how each expense was paid, and recurring series the person has dismissed.                                                                                                                                                                                | +settings, +recurring_ignored, expenses.paid_with                                    |
| v4      | what the app has learned about where a shop belongs, from the categories a person corrects by hand.                                                                                                                                                                                          | +merchant_rules                                                                      |
| v5      | committed costs — the bills that leave whether or not anyone opens the app. An amount is a timeline rather than one number, so "rent goes up in October 2027" is a row entered today (see docs/design/committed-costs.md).                                                                   | +commitments, +commitment_amounts, +commitment_settlements                           |
| v6      | savings — what a budget period has left over when it ends, plus the money a person moves in or out by hand. `amount_pence` is signed, because an overspend takes back out what earlier periods put in. The partial index keeps a period from being closed twice.                             | +savings_entries, index savings_carry_period                                         |
| v7      | what the savings are for. Goals are filled from the one savings balance in `sort_order`, so there is no second ledger to keep in step: the first goal fills first, and what is left flows to the next.                                                                                       | +savings_goals                                                                       |
| v8      | envelope budgeting. A category that finishes a period under its limit hands the difference to the next one, and an overspend is taken off it. `amount_pence` is signed and cumulative: it is everything the category has carried up to the end of `period_key`, so the chain survives a gap. | +category_carry                                                                      |

## The contract that can drift

`src/siri/budget-snapshot.ts` writes `Documents/budget-snapshot.json`;
`native/SiriInbox.swift` decodes it. Changing one side means changing the other,
and `npm run map:check` fails the build when a field Swift insists on is not
written.

- TypeScript writes **21** fields.
- Swift reads **18** of them, ignoring `generatedAt`, `weeklyReview`, `changes`.
- Fields Swift requires but nothing writes: **none**.

## Seeing it run

There is no Mac here, so the loop is:

| What                                          | How                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Logic                                         | `npm run check` — types, lint, formatting, tests                           |
| Screens                                       | `npm run preview`, then open the printed address                           |
| Siri, widget, Spotlight, notification actions | Only on a phone: build the IPA and sideload it (docs/install-on-iphone.md) |

Read the preview with page text before reaching for a screenshot; it costs a
fraction as much and says more about what is actually rendered.
